line: Jensen Huang is making his homecoming.
It hasn't even been a week since he resigned,
and the game for him to return as Nvidia's {CEO|c e o} has already
begun. It's not confirmed yet,
but the signals are so strong that everywhere,
on Twitter and across the board, this is all people are talking
about. But let's look at the facts.
According to Financial Times reports,
Jensen is meeting with his close friends to discuss and plan
how his comeback can happen. His strong allies,
the top executives across Silicon Valley,
are setting up a "war room" to put pressure on both the Board and
the White House to bring Jensen Huang back as {CEO|c e o} .
This would be good for everyone, including those top executives.
There is also a petition circulating titled "Stand with Jensen,"
which has already gathered over {180,000|one hundred eighty thousand} signatures.
Out of those, more than {9,000|nine thousand} claim to be current Nvidia
employees, meaning even Nvidia's own staff want Jensen
Huang back. Elon Musk has signed it,
Tim from Epic Games has signed it, and many other {high-profile|high profile}
figures have signed this petition. Two major investors
have already sent letters to the Board urging them to give Jensen Huang
another option to return. Trump himself stated that Jensen
is a very nice person, one of the biggest and best {CEOs|c e o s}
, and that he should be brought back. If Nvidia doesn't take him
back, Elon Musk has already said,
"It will be my honor to hire Jensen Huang."
Why? Because Elon Musk wants to go to space.
You need rockets for space, robots need chips,
electric cars need chips. The entire game revolves
around chips, and the undisputed leader in chips is Jensen
Huang. Why is everyone so keen on this?
Let me put it simply: across the entire {AI|a i} race,
Nvidia's chips are number one. Nvidia designs over
{80%|eighty percent} of them. Ever since this period began in October,
{$2 trillion|two trillion dollars} has been wiped out from Nvidia's value.
This isn't just Nvidia's loss; it impacts every company
that relies on their chips: OpenAI,
Anthropic, Elon Musk's ventures,
Oracle, and anyone needing {high-performance|high performance} silicon.
If Nvidia loses leadership like Jensen's,
these companies won't get their chips as quickly or at the same quality,
and Nvidia might lose its dominant edge to a competitor.
It hurts everyone. Now consider the other side.
The Board hasn't officially confirmed anything yet,
only stating that they are searching for a new {CEO|c e o} .
He has admitted to the affair, but investigations are still underway
regarding whether she was a spy or not.
As for the second and third affairs being reported,
he hasn't admitted to those yet. People are discussing it all over
the internet, but none of that is fully confirmed.
In my opinion, personal life and professional life are two
separate things. If it is proven that she wasn't a Chinese
spy, he deserves another chance.
Over {33|thirty three} years, he built Nvidia into a {$5 trillion|five trillion dollars}
global powerhouse, the biggest in the world.
You shouldn't dismiss someone over a single mistake.
His wife is still seen out with him; if she doesn't have an issue,
why should anyone else? What he eats at home shouldn't matter.
What matters is the value he brings to the company,
and within the company, everyone is happy with him.
My theory is that he should make a comeback,
and major industry players want the exact same thing.
If that happens, top institutional leaders will likely position
themselves early in Nvidia stock before retail investors get
the news, potentially driving a massive pump.
What do you think? Should Jensen Huang return or not?
